name: Jonas Weatherby
equipment: Heavy coat: a Lighthouse Service blue wool pea coat with the brass buttons, over the uniform he has been told to wear on Sundays and when the inspector comes
.45 automatic (his Army sidearm, kept, cleaned and against regulations), 7 in the magazine, in his sea chest
Pump shotgun (a twelve-gauge for sea ducks, bought second-hand in Rockland on the way out, because a man on a lighthouse should eat something besides salt pork)
A Lighthouse Service appointment as First Assistant Keeper, Carrow Head Light Station, effective 10 October 1924, $660 a year and quarters
The Instructions to Light-Keepers, a tin of lamp wicks, a vapor-lamp mantle wrench and a brass oil can, all of which came with the job
A first-aid kit from the Army, still with the French labels, and a pair of field glasses
A Bible from his mother, with the family's births and deaths in the front, and a pressed potato blossom
features: Up Before Dawn (Farm-Raised origin: needs only 6 hours for a long rest; can't be surprised while awake in the last hour before sunrise; advantage on saves against exhaustion from hard work, cold and lost sleep; notices without a check when animals are frightened, sick or behaving wrongly)
Held the Line (Veteran: advantage on fear checks while a conscious ally is within 10 ft of him; once per short rest, when Panic would take him at Dread 5, he acts normally instead)
Drill: Cover Man (Veteran: when a creature he can see attacks an ally within 5 ft of him, he can use his reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll; it changes no number on his sheet)
Second Wind (Veteran, 2nd level: once per short rest, as a bonus action, he regains 1d10 + 3 hit points, and loses 1 Dread if he is at Dread 3 or higher)
Service: Corpsman (Veteran, 3rd level: he carried the wounded at Seicheprey and the Argonne; he stabilises a dying creature as a bonus action, and when he does it regains 1d4 hit points)

Keeper's Log (Lighthouse Keeper background: he reads the weather and the sea a day ahead without a check, knows lamps, lenses, fog signals and flags, is welcomed by keepers, harbormasters and fishermen on any coast, and has advantage on the first fear check each night that he makes while alone)

personality.traits: I say about one word in four that other people would. When I do say something, it's usually 'ayuh' or 'that so'. I fix what's broken and I don't make a fuss about it. I am very, very hard to rattle, and I'd like it to stay that way.
personality.ideals: A light that's kept is a promise to every boat on the water that someone is awake. You keep it whether you feel like it or not, and you keep it best when nobody's looking.
personality.bonds: My mother and my two sisters on the farm at Fort Fairfield, which the bank will take in two years unless I send home enough to stop it. The men of my company in the 26th Division, the ones who came home and the ones who did not. Whatever light I'm keeping.
personality.flaws: I took a lighthouse job because I wanted to be where nobody would need me to talk about France. I don't ask for help and I don't like being thanked. If something is wrong I will try to fix it alone, at night, without telling anyone.

appearance: A tall, rawboned, fair man of thirty with big shoulders, a long Aroostook face, pale blue eyes, a slow smile, a burn scar across the back of his left hand and a voice that hardly ever gets above conversation. Lighthouse Service pea coat, wool cap, gum boots, a sea chest with his name stencilled on it.
backstory: Jonas Weatherby grew up on a potato farm at Fort Fairfield in Aroostook County, close enough to New Brunswick to see it, and went to France in 1917 with the 26th Division, the New England division, where he carried wounded men out of shell holes at Seicheprey and the Argonne and never once talked about it afterwards. He came home in 1919 to a farm with a mortgage and a father who had died that winter, and worked it for four years and lost money every one of them. In 1923 he passed the Lighthouse Service examination, because a keeper earns cash every month and spends almost none of it, and kept a light on a Casco Bay ledge for a year without complaint. In September the Lighthouse Service's district office in Portland offered him First Assistant at Carrow Head, because the last assistant, a Rockland man named Pottle, quit without notice and went home and would not say why. Jonas said yes the same day. (Hook: in the assistant's quarters at the Light, behind the washstand, Pottle left a note in pencil: 'You hear a bell under the water on the big tides, it isn't the fog bell. Don't go down to the Point. Ask Oren about his father's log.' Jonas will find it the first night.)
